item.text:
## Accepted Evidence Records

All accepted records below were opened and read. I excluded snippet-only or inaccessible candidates from acceptance.

| ID | Title / publisher / date / URL | Locator | Claim summary | Source type | Temporal fit | Putin attribution | Contrary / limiting evidence | 2B lenses |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2B-001` | **THE SECRETARY-GENERAL -- PRESS REMARKS ON THE BLACK SEA INITIATIVE AND MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING ON FACILITATING EXPORTS OF RUSSIAN FOOD PRODUCTS AND FERTILIZERS** / United Nations in Ukraine / 17 Jul 2023 / [URL](https://ukraine.un.org/en/239708-secretary-general-press-remarks-black-sea-initiative-and-memorandum-understanding) | [L72-L79](https://ukraine.un.org/en/239708-secretary-general-press-remarks-black-sea-initiative-and-memorandum-understanding) | The UN says Russia terminated the Black Sea Initiative and withdrew security guarantees, ending a channel that had moved over 32 million metric tons of food and reduced prices. | UN institutional statement | High | Indirect, state-level decision attributable to Putin’s government; not a direct Putin quote | UN also says it had been working to resolve Russian export obstacles and had sent a proposal to Putin; that narrows, but does not erase, Russian agency in the withdrawal. | 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.10 |
| `2B-002` | **Statement on the Cabinet Meeting of 21 June 2023** / The Presidency of the Republic of South Africa / 21 Jun 2023 / [URL](https://www.presidency.gov.za/node/7157) | [L74-L79](https://www.presidency.gov.za/node/7157) | South Africa’s cabinet reported that Putin and Zelensky both welcomed the African peace initiative and committed to further engagements on de-escalation, POWs, children, and humanitarian corridors. | Government statement / diplomatic summary | High | Indirect via third-party official summary of the meeting | This is South Africa’s account, not a Kremlin transcript; it supports diplomatic engagement but not substantive Russian concessions. | 2B.1, 2B.7 |
| `2B-003` | **President Ramaphosa presses Africa's proposal for a path to peace** / The Presidency of the Republic of South Africa / 18 Jun 2023 / [URL](https://www.presidency.gov.za/president-ramaphosa-presses-africas-proposal-path-peace) | [L62-L68](https://www.presidency.gov.za/president-ramaphosa-presses-africas-proposal-path-peace) | Africa’s mission said it had laid out a path to peace built around de-escalation, POWs/children, UN Charter sovereignty, humanitarian aid, and reconstruction. | Government statement / diplomatic summary | High | Indirect; describes the mission Putin received, not Putin’s own words | It reflects mediator framing, not a concession by Putin; still useful as evidence that diplomacy was on the table in 2023. | 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.10 |
| `2B-004` | **Economic Activity in Europe and Central Asia Improves but Growth Lags Pre-Pandemic Levels** / World Bank / 5 Oct 2023 / [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/10/05/economic-activity-in-europe-and-central-asia-improves-but-growth-lags-pre-pandemic-levels) | [L59-L68](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/10/05/economic-activity-in-europe-and-central-asia-improves-but-growth-lags-pre-pandemic-levels) | Russia’s 2023 growth was boosted by a surge in government spending on the military and social transfers; the World Bank still described the outlook as weak and constrained. | International financial institution press release | High | Indirect, macro-level consequence of Putin-era policy rather than a direct motive statement | Growth alone does not prove regime motive, but the military-spending channel is directly relevant to mobilization and wartime prioritization. | 2B.8, 2B.10 |
| `2B-005` | **Human rights situation during the Russian occupation of territory of Ukraine and its aftermath, 24 February 2022 to 31 December 2023** / OHCHR / 20 Mar 2024 / [URL](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/2024-04/2024-03-20%20OHCHR%20Report%20on%20Occupation%20and%20Aftermath_EN.pdf) | [L70-L99](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/2024-04/2024-03-20%20OHCHR%20Report%20on%20Occupation%20and%20Aftermath_EN.pdf) | OHCHR found persistent patterns of IHL/IHRL violations in occupied territory, including arbitrary detention, torture, killings, repression, and forced institutional replacement. | UN thematic monitoring report | High, but retrospective to end-2023 | Indirect but strong: the report attributes conduct to Russian armed forces and occupying authorities under Russian control | Retrospective report; Russia denied access to occupied territory and detainees, so fact-finding is necessarily constrained. | 2B.2, 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.9, 2B.10 |
| `2B-006` | Same report as above | [L111-L124](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/2024-04/2024-03-20%20OHCHR%20Report%20on%20Occupation%20and%20Aftermath_EN.pdf) | OHCHR says former DPR/LPR armed groups were formally integrated into Russian structures from 1 Jan 2023 and that Wagner contractors were under overall Russian control. | UN thematic monitoring report | High, retrospective to 2023 | Indirect but explicit control attribution to the Russian Federation | OHCHR is careful to describe “overall control” rather than individually assign every action to Putin personally. | 2B.2, 2B.5, 2B.9 |
| `2B-007` | Same report as above | [L1180-L1184](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/2024-04/2024-03-20%20OHCHR%20Report%20on%20Occupation%20and%20Aftermath_EN.pdf) | Russian authorities required lists of men eligible for conscription and summoned young men in occupied territory, creating a risk of conscription into the Russian armed forces. | UN thematic monitoring report | High, retrospective to 2023 | Indirect state/control attribution | This concerns occupied territory and coercive administration, not ordinary Russian domestic conscription alone. | 2B.2, 2B.5, 2B.8 |
| `2B-008` | **Attack on Funeral Reception in Hroza, 5 October 2023** / OHCHR / 5 Oct 2023 / [URL](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/attack-funeral-reception-hroza-EN) | [L82-L86](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/attack-funeral-reception-hroza-EN) | OHCHR found reasonable grounds to believe Russian forces struck a civilian funeral reception, killing 59 civilians, and urged Russia to acknowledge responsibility and investigate. | UN monitoring report | High | Indirect but specific to Russian armed forces | Standard is “reasonable grounds,” not a court judgment; still strong evidence of civilian-harm risk and alleged unlawful attack. | 2B.4, 2B.6, 2B.9, 2B.10 |
| `2B-009` | **Civilian Deaths In Ukraine War Top 10,000, UN Says** / OHCHR / 21 Nov 2023 / [URL](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/civilian-deaths-ukraine-war-top-10000-un-says-UA) | [L78-L86](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/civilian-deaths-ukraine-war-top-10000-un-says-UA) | HRMMU said at least 10,000 civilians had been killed and warned the war risked becoming a protracted conflict, with attacks far from the frontlines leaving no place safe. | UN monitoring update | High | Indirect, war-wide but clearly tied to Russia’s full-scale invasion | The casualty figure is verified by HRMMU methodology and likely understates reality; it does not by itself prove intent, but it does show cumulative harm. | 2B.2, 2B.4, 2B.10 |
| `2B-010` | **Cluster Munition Use in Russia-Ukraine War** / Human Rights Watch / 29 May 2023 / [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/05/29/cluster-munition-use-russia-ukraine-war) | [L607-L612](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/05/29/cluster-munition-use-russia-ukraine-war) and [L739-L745](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/05/29/cluster-munition-use-russia-ukraine-war) | HRW says Russian forces used cluster munitions in attacks causing hundreds of civilian casualties; it also notes Russia did not deny use and instead defended cluster munitions as legitimate. | NGO investigation / briefing | High | Indirect, but strongly tied to Russian armed forces and Russian public justification | HRW is not a court, and it also documents Ukrainian cluster-munition use; that context does not negate the Russian-use finding. | 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.6, 2B.9 |
| `2B-011` | Same HRW briefing as above | [L743-L747](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/05/29/cluster-munition-use-russia-ukraine-war) | HRW reports Russia avoided direct comment on its own use and instead described cluster munitions as a legitimate weapon with defense value, which is a deflective public-defense posture. | NGO quoting state response | High | Indirect; this is Russia’s position as summarized by HRW, not a Kremlin transcript | This is still useful for the justification lens, but a direct Kremlin or ministry source would be better. | 2B.3, 2B.6 |
| `2B-012` | **Putin says Wagner mutiny is 'treason' in televised address** / Reuters via Investing.com / 24 Jun 2023 / [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-wagner-mutiny-is-treason-in-televised-address-3112381) | [L406-L427](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-wagner-mutiny-is-treason-in-televised-address-3112381) | Reuters reports Putin labeled the Wagner uprising treason and said he would do everything to protect Russia and stabilize Rostov-on-Don. | Wire report on a direct Putin address | High | Direct reporting of Putin’s televised remarks | Secondary reporting, but on a contemporaneous address; useful for command/control and proxy discipline. | 2B.5, 2B.9, 2B.10 |

## Provisional Lens-by-Lens Map

- `2B.1` Diplomacy / de-escalation: `2B-001`, `2B-002`, `2B-003`, `2B-012`
- `2B.2` Initiation / expansion / prolongation / coercion / proxies: `2B-005`, `2B-006`, `2B-007`, `2B-008`, `2B-009`, `2B-010`
- `2B.3` Defensive necessity vs prestige / regime survival: `2B-004`, `2B-011`
- `2B.4` Civilian protection / IHL: `2B-005`, `2B-008`, `2B-009`, `2B-010`
- `2B.5` Restraint and responsibility for forces / proxies: `2B-005`, `2B-006`, `2B-007`, `2B-010`, `2B-012`
- `2B.6` Truthful vs manipulative public justification: `2B-008`, `2B-010`, `2B-011`
- `2B.7` Ceasefires / negotiations / lawful settlements / reconciliation: `2B-001`, `2B-002`, `2B-003`
- `2B.8` Military spending and mobilization motives: `2B-004`, `2B-007`
- `2B.9` Accountability for failures / civilian harm / illegal conduct: `2B-005`, `2B-006`, `2B-008`, `2B-010`, `2B-012`
- `2B.10` Net change in peace / stability / legality: `2B-001`, `2B-003`, `2B-004`, `2B-005`, `2B-008`, `2B-009`, `2B-012`

## Exact Gaps Remaining

- Direct 2023 Kremlin-language primary transcripts still need retrieval. The key missing items are Putin’s Federal Assembly address, his China joint statement, and his African-peace-meeting remarks.
- I still need a direct Russian primary record on Putin’s own explanation for the Black Sea withdrawal and the broader war aims, not just third-party summaries.
- ICC access remains blocked from this browser path, so the arrest-warrant legal record is still not directly extractable here.
- The current set is strong on civilian harm and coercive occupation, but thinner on:
  - explicit Putin-side claims of defensive necessity,
  - any genuine 2023 de-escalation step beyond exploratory talks,
  - direct Russian-language statements on ceasefire terms,
  - and detailed 2023 Russian budget/mobilization materials.
- For the peace/settlement lens, the strongest available evidence is mediated and third-party. A direct Kremlin transcript would materially improve confidence.
